summary.text: 边 is the simplified form of 邊, commonly meaning a side, edge, margin, or border. Analyses of 邊’s early structure differ: one assigns movement meaning to 辵, while another assigns “beside” to 方; proposed sound elements also vary.

formation.text: 邊’s formation is disputed. The Han-era dictionary analysis treats 辵 (written 辶 in the component position) as semantic, suggesting movement, and 𦤝 as phonetic. Another analysis assigns “beside” to 方 and proposes sound roles for 自 and 丙. 边 is the simplified form of 邊.

components.text: In one analysis of traditional 邊, 辵 contributes movement meaning; 辶 is its conventional side form. That role is not established for 辶 in simplified 边.
The Han-era dictionary analysis identifies 𦤝 as the sound element in 邊. Another account places 臱 in 邊’s sound series, but the graphic relation between 𦤝 and 臱 is unresolved.

sound_limitation.text: The evidence gives 邊’s fanqie 布賢切 but does not establish that 臱 and 𦤝 are the same component. Without that graphic link or a reading for 𦤝, no component-to-character sound comparison can be established.

components.text: One analysis of the bronze form of 邊 assigns 方 the sense “beside.” This differs from the account that assigns a movement role to 辵.
Some analyses propose that 自 marks sound in early 邊, but no comparable ancient reading for 自 in this character is supplied.

sound_limitation.text: Although a phonetic role is proposed, no source-specific ancient pronunciation for 自 in 邊 is given. Reconstructions for 邊 or 臱 do not provide that comparison.

components.text: Some analyses propose that 丙 marks sound in early 邊. It is absent from 边; no comparable ancient reading for 丙 in this character is supplied.

sound_limitation.text: Although a phonetic role is proposed, no source-specific ancient pronunciation for 丙 in 邊 is given. Reconstructions for 邊 or 臱 do not provide that comparison.

components.text: In 边, 辶 is the conventional side form of 辵. The simplified graph preserves this shape, but its role in 边 is not established by the traditional-form analyses.

history.text: The curated oracle-style, bronze-style, and Chu silk-style redraws show separate script traditions for 邊; they do not establish a sequence among the forms.

边 is the simplified counterpart of 邊. An account describes an internal change from 臱 to 力 during simplification, but the precise graphic steps remain unresolved; the proposed 1956 adoption date has not been verified against an inspected primary scheme document.

uncertainties.text: Early analyses disagree: one assigns movement meaning to 辵 and sound to 𦤝; others assign “beside” to 方 and propose sound roles for 自 and 丙. The accounts do not resolve which analysis best explains the early graph.
One account calls 臱 the original graph, but it remains unresolved whether 臱 is a direct graphic ancestor of 邊 or whether the earliest form was already 邊.
Reconstructions for 邊 and 臱 come from different systems and cannot be combined. Comparable ancient pronunciation evidence for the proposed sound elements 自 and 丙 is not supplied.

The curated drawings do not establish a direct sequence: the oracle- and bronze-style redraws are not tied to specific dated artifacts, and the cited silk manuscript image was not independently examined.

senses.text: One analysis proposes “beside” as an original sense of 邊; its earliest attestation and date are unresolved.
A bronze-inscription context is reported with the meaning “frontier region”; its date and place in the development of the senses are unresolved.
边 and 邊 commonly refer to a side or edge, including a margin or border. A dated first occurrence or continuous development from “beside” is unresolved.

senses.gloss: while, in the paired construction 邊…邊…
senses.text: 邊 is also recorded in the paired construction 邊…邊…, meaning “while.” Its chronology and development from spatial senses are unresolved.

limitations.text: No securely dated first occurrence for each sense, or documented continuous development from “beside” through “frontier” or “edge” to the paired “while” construction, is established.

overview.text: 边 is the simplified form of 邊, commonly used for a side or edge. Analyses of 邊’s early structure disagree: one assigns meaning to movement, another to “beside,” and proposed sound elements remain uncertain.
